title: Protocol for live enhanced resolution confocal imaging of dendritic spinule dynamics in primary mouse cortical neuron culture
protocol: Prepare NB transfection medium and pre-warm it to 37°C in an H2O bath.
Pass the prepared media through a 0.22 μm filter using a sterile syringe.
Add 100 μL of Opti-MEM 1× to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Add 50 μL of Opti-MEM 1× to another tube (set of 2 tubes per imaging dish).
Add 7 μL of LFA2K to the first tube containing 100 μL of Opti-MEM 1×.
Add 4 μg of DNA per plasmid, i.e., p-mRuby-N1 or p-GFP, to the second tube containing 50 μL of Opti-MEM 1×.
Transfer contents of the Opti-MEM + LFA2K tube to the plasmid DNA tube using a 200 μL pipette tip.
Pipette up and down steadily 30 times to mix LFA2K and plasmid DNA.
Transport closed tubes to 37°C with 5% CO2 incubator, open the caps, and incubate for 20-30 min to facilitate LFA2K-DNA complex formation.
Transfect dissociated cortical neuron cultures with fluorescent protein-encoding plasmid(s).
Using a 1 mL pipette tip, remove neuronal conditioned media and reserve it in a 15 mL conical tube.
Keep the reserved conditioned media at 37°C.
Gently add 1.75 mL of pre-warmed, antibiotic-free NB transfection media to the inside edge of a dish.
Add contents of the Eppendorf tube containing LFA2K-DNA complexes drop-by-drop using a 1 mL pipette tip.
Gently mix by rocking the imaging dish up and down and then back and forth.
Incubate imaging dishes in a humidified incubator at 37°C with 5% CO2 for 3–4 h.
Replace transfection media containing complexes with ½ conditioned media and ½ NB + supplements + 1× APV medium.
Position a glass pipette tip along the inside edge of the dish.
Carefully use suction to remove all transfection media without disrupting the neuronal network.
Add 1.5 mL of reserved, pre-warmed neuron-conditioned medium and 1 mL of NB + supplements + 1× APV medium.
Incubate dishes in a humidified incubator at 37°C with 5% CO2 for ~48 h.
Optional: Transfect cells with p-mRuby-N1 (red) and pCAG_PSD95.FingR-eGFP-CCR5TC (green).
Optional: Transfect neurons with p-mRuby-N1 (red) and pGP-CMV-GCAMP6s (green).
Optimize confocal parameters for enhanced resolution spinule imaging.
Set up Nikon A1R HD microscope with resonant scanning and GaAsP multi-detector unit.
Use Plan Apo Lambda 100× 1.45 NA oil objective for imaging.
Employ 488/561 nm excitation lasers for optimal signal.
Collect data with appropriate S/N, sample spacing, and proper deconvolution.
Use piezo-electric positioner with nanometer resolution and repeatability.
Acquire high precision Z-stacks to track individual spinules.
Set up environmental chamber for live imaging according to standard protocol.
Turn on Tokai Hit stage top incubation system to maintain 37°C temperature.
Open 5% CO2 tank valve to ensure proper CO2 level in the environmental chamber.
Check for water in humidifier if using an incubation system without gas mixer.
Switch to the Plan Apo Lambda 100× 1.45 NA oil objective and attach the objective heat collar.
Add one drop of oil to the 100× 1.45 NA objective.
Attach environmental chamber insert to the stage base.
Mount a 35 mm dish containing healthy transfected pyramidal excitatory neurons onto the environmental chamber stage securely.
Find the sample plane of focus at 20× magnification.
Select eye port for ocular viewing using an X-Cite 120 Fluorescence LED Illumination System with FITC filter cube.
Scan the entire glass area for healthy, brightly fluorescing neurons.
Save each X/Y coordinate demarking a neuron’s location by navigating to the ND Acquisition tab and XY sub-tab under Point Name.
Assess neuron health prior to live imaging to avoid cells showing signs of plasma membrane blebbing or dendrite deterioration.
Switch to the 100× 1.45 NA objective.
Adjust focus.
If more oil is needed, carefully remove environmental stage with the sample still securely attached.
Select Resonant scanning detector button.
Choose a scan speed of ½ frame per second.
Adjust the pinhole to 0.6 airy units.
Select a pixel size of 1/2 Nyquist suggested sampling size.
Use X= 0.06 μm, Y= 0.06 μm, Z=0.12 μm for pixel dimensions.
Set scan area to 1024 pixels (width) × 512 pixels (height).
Use Scan or Capture mode to adjust field of view, centering on the secondary branches of apical neuronal dendrites.
Adjust laser power, PMT gain (named as HV by the software), and offset for each channel.
Achieve optimal S/N for enhanced resolution spinule imaging in the sample.
Acquire confocal images at approximately 10 seconds per stack for a duration between 10 minutes and 1 hour.
Open NIS Elements AR software, version 5.211 or later.
Navigate to the File tab, select Open folder, and open an ND2 file previously acquired in NIS-Elements.
Go to the Deconvolution tab and choose 3D Deconvolution from the drop-down menu.
Select automatic deconvolution method under the General tab.
Ensure that parameters such as Modality, Magnification, Pinhole Size, NA, Immersion Ref. Index, Calibration, Z-step auto-populate correctly.
Choose create new document for output settings.
Check the box for each channel to be deconvolved under Channels, e.g., 488, 568, 647.
Verify that ‘do not subtract’ is selected under Advanced Settings tab, Preprocessing.
Verify that ‘Compute PSF automatically’ is selected under Point Spread Function.
Click the Deconvolve button to begin deconvolving.
